reason: The cited evidence supports grain refinement and yield strength increase from 75% cold rolling in a similar Ti-rich alloy, and shows high pitting potentials with a TiO2/Nb2O5 oxide, but it does not address room-temperature creep resistance, controlled isothermal oxidation, or the specific Ti68Nb7Ta3Zr4Mo18 composition, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: Severe cold rolling (≈75% reduction) refines grain structure and increases yield strength in Ti-rich alloys
Cold rolling plus controlled oxidation produces a uniform passive oxide layer of TiO2 and Nb2O5
Ultrafine grain structure improves room-temperature creep resistance by impeding dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding
A uniform passive oxide layer significantly enhances corrosion resistance
The specific alloy Ti68Nb7Ta3Zr4Mo18 responds to cold rolling and oxidation similarly to the cited Ti80–Nb10–Mo5–Sn5 alloy
